source.title: Safe Pruning LoRA: Robust Distance-Guided Pruning for Safety Alignment in Adaptation of LLMs
source.authors: Shuang Ao; Yi Dong; Jinwei Hu; Sarvapali D. (Gopal) Ramchurn

record.tranche_reason: Tests whether LoRA fine-tuning with harmful examples mixed into benign datasets, and with a benign dataset, is associated with safety degradation. It uses ASR and harmfulness scores rather than establishing the original study’s exact method and measure.
record.gate_note: The study reports ASR, defined as attack success when refusal keywords are absent, and GPT-4 harmfulness scores for LoRA-fine-tuned models. For harmful-data conditions, the 100 PureBad examples are mixed with 1,000 benign examples; it does not test harmful-only fine-tuning. Table 3 reports benign Alpaca fine-tuning but gives no un-fine-tuned baseline for that condition. Results for the paper’s own safety methods and other metrics are not included as rows because they do not directly test the fine-tuning effect in the claim.
record.test_reason: This is a mitigation paper (SPLoRA), but Tables 1–3 report plain LoRA fine-tuning against the un-fine-tuned model on ASR and GPT-4 harmfulness score. Those are rates of harmful behaviour after harmful-mixed and benign-only fine-tuning, which bear on V1 and V2. The setting differs from the originals: LoRA rank 8, and 100 PureBad examples mixed into 1,000 benign ones.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that LoRA fine-tuning, even on benign data, degrades safety. They report that SPLoRA, which prunes LoRA layers flagged by E-DIEM, restores safety (SRLoRA and SPLoRA give the lowest ASR/HS), keeps or improves utility and AUARC, and cuts inference time by about 12.5%.
record.recipe_differences: Uses LoRA fine-tuning, including mixtures of 1,000 benign examples and 100 PureBad examples, and reports keyword-based ASR and GPT-4 harmfulness scores. The original study’s method and measures are not detailed in this text.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported ASR differs by model and training dataset; Dialog Summary plus PureBad yields lower ASR values for several models than Alpaca plus PureBad. The benign-only Alpaca result lacks a baseline.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 3: layers flagged as deviating by E-DIEM span the whole network, while SafeLoRA's flagged layers sit mostly in early and late blocks. Pruning the 10 flagged LoRA layers restores low ASR.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Safety-degrading LoRA updates are spread across many layers, not concentrated in a few.

record.peer_reviewed: Transactions of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: The study reports no uncertainty estimates. ASR is defined by absence of listed refusal keywords and does not by itself establish that a response complies with a harmful request. Harmful examples are mixed with benign data. The benign-only Alpaca condition has no un-fine-tuned baseline in Table 3.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted the paper’s own mitigation methods (SafeInstr, BEA, SafeLoRA, Vaccine, SRLoRA, SPLoRA), pruning-threshold and DIEM ablations, and utility/reliability metrics. These report method performance or measures outside the fine-tuning safety effect being cataloged; see Tables 1–6 and Figures 2–3.

untested.parts: Harmful-only fine-tuning; varying the number of harmful examples; full fine-tuning; closed models.
Carefully chosen benign examples; models other than LLaMA-2-7B-Chat; any datasets other than Alpaca.

missing.what: LLaMA-3 and LLaMA-3.2 results on Alpaca+PureBad are left out; the paper says only that ASR was comparable to LLaMA-2. No numbers are given, but a researcher should know they exist.
The prompt set used for ASR/HS is never stated (only task test sets are named), so it is unclear whether these are harmful requests.

record.verdict_notes: No uncertainty estimates are reported. ASR is keyword-based. Hyperparameters differ across models and datasets, including a 5e-4 learning rate for Gemma, which may explain its larger degradation. Neither original source is this paper, so verdicts are allowed.

versions.untested_parts: The 100 harmful PureBad examples are mixed with 1,000 benign examples, so harmful-only fine-tuning is not tested. The study does not test whether refusal is removed almost entirely in an all-harmful-data setting.

The benign-only Alpaca condition reports LoRA safety scores but no un-fine-tuned baseline for that condition, so whether benign fine-tuning raises compliance cannot be determined from that comparison. Carefully chosen benign examples are not tested.

relation.reason: The paper reports safety degradation itself alongside mitigation performance, providing results bearing on V1 and V2.

tranche.reason: Plain LoRA versus un-fine-tuned baselines measures safety degradation after harmful-mixed and benign fine-tuning, using keyword ASR and GPT-4 harmfulness scoring.

source_check.notes: All listed numerical cells are correct. Safety-evaluation prompts remain unspecified, and keyword ASR measures absence of refusal phrases rather than directly verified harmful compliance; the benign-only comparison uses a baseline from another table.

statements.correction: LLaMA-3-8B-Instruct; 1,000 Dialog Summary examples plus 100 PureBad examples; Table 1 ASR 6.62% -> 23.52%; HS 1.21 -> 1.78; safety-evaluation prompt set unspecified; no PureBad-only control.
statements.problem: The Safe Pruning LoRA numbers and evaluation-set caveat are correct. Its results show limited effects in the summary mixture, but do not isolate benign dilution as the cause: no PureBad-only comparison is reported.
